item.title: Arman Tsarukyan attacks Dillon Danis igniting near riot at RAF 14 press conference
item.description: Arman Tsarukyan was clarly not amused by Dillon Danis’ choice of apparel at the RAF 14 press conference on Thursday. After exchanging plenty of trash talk in a calm manner, Danis stood to show off his t-shirt when asked what he was wearing. Danis, who is never short on controversy, revealed he was wearing a customized shirt featuring Tsarukyan’s teammate and friend Khamzat Chimaev. “It says Khamzat’s my bitch,” Danis responded. “And it has a picture with him without a beard.” A second later, Tsarukyan stood from his seat and charged at Danis looking to either silence the always outspoken grappling veteran or perhaps to take the shirt off him. Whatever the reason, Tsarukyan’s mad dash at Danis ignited a huge brawl as dozens of people charged the stage either in support of the fighters or security trying to keep them separated. The melee nearly tore down the stage as RAF officials attempted to gain control of the situation with Danis and Tsarukyan looking for punches rather than takedowns. When RAF officials finally gained control of the situation, the stage was cleared for the customary faceoffs but needles to say Tsarukyan and Danis did not appear again. Tsarukyan and Danis meet in the RAF 14 main event on Friday, which kicks off at 9 p.m. ET with full coverage on MMA Fighting.

item.title: George Russell responds to Christian Horner's Red Bull simulator claim
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has responded to former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner's claims that he, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri used to pay to use the Milton Keynes outfit's simulators. Horner, who was dismissed from Red Bull last year, said on the High Performance podcast this week that all three drivers had paid to use the team's simulator when they were younger. According to Horner, the person running the simulator told him the three young drivers were better than those Red Bull already had, but Helmut Marko was not interested in signing them. "I remember George Russell was paying us to go on our simulator, as was Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Their dads were writing cheques for them to run on the driver simulator that we had," Horner said. "And the guy that was looking after it was coming up to me and saying, 'Christian, these kids are better than the juniors we've got at the moment.' I remember taking them to Helmut and going, 'Look, I really think you should look at these guys.'" George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes Russell, who currently sits second in the drivers' championship, was asked about Horner's comments while speaking to the media ahead of the United States Grand Prix. "So back in 2013, simulators weren't really a thing for anybody," the British driver explained. "Any junior teams didn't have simulators and there was an opportunity to do some driving on that simulator in the Formula Renault car, so it was more as preparation for testing and driving for the series that we were racing because, as I said, no teams had it. So that's the extent of it. That's all I'll say." The United States Grand Prix is scheduled for 23-25 October at the Circuit of the Americas and kicks off the penultimate triple-header of the season. item.description: WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert speaks prior to Game 1 of a WNBA basketball final playoff series between the Las Vegas Aces and the Phoenix Mercury, Oct. 3, 2025, in Las Vegas. | John Locher WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert inally gave a clear response to Republican lawmakers seeking a clearer definition of the league’s eligibility criteria, saying former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White can’t play in the league because both are men. “With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men,” Engelbert wrote in an Oct. 16 letter reported by OutKick . The response came after Indiana Rep. Marlin Stutzman and a few other Republicans in a September letter pushed the league to define what a woman is and explain why Freedom and White couldn’t join the WNBA draft in 2027. Huh Freedom’s effort to enter the league has also spilled into the stands. In August, he attended a game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. Freedom recently made another attempt to attend a game Wednesday, trying to go to Game 3 of the WNBA Finals where the Atlanta Dream were playing the Golden State Valkyries. Both teams are chasing the first championship in franchise history, while young stars like Angel Reese are continuing to grow before fans’ eyes. With so much on the line, the basketball deserves to be the biggest story. The competing views have made eligibility a recurring subject of discussion even as the league continues to grow its audience and expand its footprint . Engelbert, who announced in September that she plans to retire at the end of the season, is also responding to the latest questions during the final months of her tenure. Her letter provides a direct answer about Freedom and White’s eligibility, but the broader question of how the WNBA defines its rules remains part of a debate that has extended well beyond the two former NBA players.

item.title: Pat Murphy Pumps Brakes on Brandon Woodruff’s Possible Return
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 22: Brandon Woodruff #53 of the Milwaukee Brewers speaks to media at a press conference during a workout day prior to game on of the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on October 22, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Brewers are close to starting the World Series. Game 1 against the Tampa Bay Rays will be on Friday night, and the Brewers will hope to take advantage of being at home to start the series. However, there are still a couple of things the Brewers need to figure out before setting their roster. The biggest question mark right now is whether Brandon Woodruff will be able to pitch. He has recovered well from his injury and is healthy enough to be on the roster, but one problem remains. If he gets hurt again, the Brewers cannot replace him according to MLB rules. Manager Pat Murphy was asked about the possibility of Woodruff being active, and while he seems open to the idea of having him, he also made sure to pump the brakes a bit. “Obviously it would be great for him, the organization, and he could help us,” Murphy said. “It’s a seven-game series, there’s no man on second in extra innings. item.title: Free Miller Lite during the World Series offered by Molson Coors
item.description: The first Miller Lite to celebrate the Milwaukee Brewers return to the World Series is on Molson Coors. For Game 1 of the series between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays the company is providing one free beer to Wisconsin residents purchased on Oct. 23. The company announced that anyone 21 years or older can receive a rebate for one 16-ounce or larger beer purchased on Oct. 23. Customers have until Nov. 4 to claim the rebate. Those who are interested in the rebate can go to the company's website and provide the store name, date of purchase, and items purchased for rebate are showing clearly on the receipt in a photo. If you are unable to get the whole receipt in one image, you can provide a second picture. Game 1 of the World Series is scheduled for Oct. 23 at 7 p.m. Molson Coors is also marking Brewers’ playoff run, with free brewery tours of the historic Miller Brewery on Oct. 23. A total of 120 visitors will have the opportunity to experience one of two complimentary 75-minute tours scheduled for 12 p.m. and 12:30 p.m. The first 120 people in line at the Miller Brewery Visitor’s Center at 4251 W. State St., will receive free admission and a commemorative Miller Lite Brewers hat. The tour takes 60 people maximum, so the first two hours are free. Tours, which typically cost $20, include three beer samples for guests 21 and older with valid identification. The first 30 fans in line who don't secure a tour spot will still receive a commemorative hat, while supplies last. “As a longtime neighbor, supporter and proud beer sponsor of the Milwaukee Brewers, Miller Lite is raising a glass to this historic moment alongside Brewers fans across Wisconsin,” Alison Hanrahan, community affairs manager for the Miller Brewery, said in a statement. “We can’t think of a better way to toast the Brewers’ incredible run than with beer and tours of the brewery we proudly call home.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Free Miller Lite during the World Series offered by Molson Coors

item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers passes in the second half during the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received more encouraging news Thursday as quarterback Baker Mayfield participated fully in practice for the second consecutive day ahead of Sunday’s NFC South matchup against the Carolina Panthers. Mayfield, who has missed the last three games after dislocating his right thumb in Week 3, continues to make progress toward a potential return. The veteran quarterback was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday, providing optimism that he could be back under center when Tampa Bay travels to Carolina. Although Mayfield has yet to be officially named the starter, his participation throughout the week is a positive development for a Buccaneers team looking to snap its recent struggles. Elsewhere on the injury report, running back Bucky Irving (illness) and cornerback Zyon McCollum (illness) were upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey (illness) also improved to full participation. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf), and linebacker Christian Rozeboom (finger) remained sidelined for a second consecutive day. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. was also held out for rest. For Carolina, outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Thomas Incoom (calf) remained out of practice Thursday. Running back Chuba Hubbard, linebacker Devin Lloyd, offensive tackle Taylor Moton, and tight end Darren Waller all returned as full participants after receiving rest Wednesday. item.title: UConn targets, 2 CIAC teams to play in inaugural Hoophall Classic Girls Showcase in Springfield, Mass.
item.description: Kaleena Smith #11 of the Ontario Christian Knights celebrates as they defeated the Archbishop Mitty Monarchs 56-49 to win a girls Open Division CIF State basketball game at the Golden 1 Center in Sacramento on Saturday, March 14, 2026. (Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group via Getty Images) Two Connecticut girls basketball teams and at least two UConn women's basketball recruits have been selected to compete in the inaugural Panini Hoophall Classic Girls' Showcase on Jan. 15-16 at Western New England University in Springfield, Massachusetts. The event will feature 15 games over two days, with 21 teams from 11 states and Canada and 44 nationally ranked prospects. Among them are the top two prospects in ESPN's Class of 2027 rankings - Kaleena Smith from Ontario Christian (Calif.) and Ivanna Wilson-Manyacka from the Bullis School (Md.), both of whom received in-home visits from UConn coaches . Their teams are each scheduled to play twice during the showcase, and back-to-back on Jan. 15. Sacred Heart Academy and Northwest Catholic will compete in the showcase on Saturday, Jan. 16, at Western New England University. This will be the first Hoophall weekend with two full days dedicated to girls basketball. Last year, the original Hoophall Classic at Springfield College devoted one full day to the sport. Northwest Catholic and Sacred Heart Academy finished second and third, respectively, in the GametimeCT Final Top 10 poll last March . Northwest Catholic defeated Sacred Heart Academy in the CIAC Division I semifinals, then lost in the final to Greenwich. Sacred Heart Academy plays on Jan. 16 at 10:30 a.m. against Andover (Mass.), and Northwest Catholic follows at noon against DePaul Prep (N.J.). Tickets for the inaugural Panini Hoophall Classic Girls' Showcase are on sale at etix.com . Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. item.title: Marco Sturm Explains Bruins' Decision to Bench Young Players Late vs. Stars
item.description: Marco Sturm Explains Bruins' Decision to Bench Young Players Late vs. Stars originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Boston Bruins head coach Marco Sturm had a specific reason for keeping several of his young players off the ice during the final minutes of Tuesday's game against the Dallas Stars. During media availability Thursday, Scott McLaughlin asked Sturm about his decision to keep James Hagens, Matt Poitras and other young Bruins forwards off the ice late in regulation against Dallas. Sturm said he had read McLaughlin’s article about the decision and explained that the atmosphere in Dallas and the momentum shift after the Stars tied the game influenced his thinking. I asked Sturm about this today (not using a few of the kids in the final 5-ish minutes in Dallas). Turns out he read the article. Thought his explanation was insightful, so here it is in full. Cited the environment in Dallas and the way he felt the game turn after they tied it. https://t.co/1OdrxZntHT — Scott McLaughlin (@smclaughlin9) October 22, 2026 "I want to help them to grow in getting into those situations, and our situations, I'm going to put them out there," Sturm told reporters Thursday. "But if you're in Dallas, and if you've ever been in Dallas, it's one of the toughest buildings." The Bruins held a lead before Dallas scored to tie the game, changing the feel of the contest in the closing minutes. Sturm said he sensed the shift and wanted to protect his younger players from being thrown into a difficult situation. "When they scored, there was a big change," Sturm said. The two will put those belts on the line on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026 at San Antonio's Frost Bank Center. (Courtesy photo/Top Rank) O'Shaquie Foster and Emanuel Navarrete are two champions pigeon-holed by boxing fans who have quite rigid opinions about the styles of both fighters. The common thought is that Foster, who grew up in Orange but lives and trains in Houston , is the slick boxer, who thinks his way around the ring and relies on his defense and superior technique to win fights. Navarrete is regarded as the stereotypical brazen Mexican fighter looking for knockouts. O'Shaquie Foster vs. Emanuel Navarrete When: 7 p.m. Saturday (main card) Where: Frost Bank Center, San Antonio Streaming: DAZN Tickets: $68-$500 at Ticketmaster Whether those preconceived definitions are perfect fits or not, both fighters have found their way to the top of the junior lightweight division in their own ways. Foster (25-3, 12 KOs) is the 130-pound World Boxing Council champion who has successfully defended that belt two straight times by winning dominating decisions over Stephen Fulton and Raymond Ford . Navarrete (40-2-1, 33 KOs) is a three-division champion, working his way up to junior lightweight where he holds the World Boxing Organization and International Boxing Federation titles with two straight knockouts to hold on to those belts. Those styles will clash with all three belts on the line when the two meet Saturday night at San Antonio's Frost Bank Center . "He wants someone that's going to sit in front of him and I think my style is a little bit more difficult," the 33-year-old Foster said Thursday. "We're here now, so we'll see Saturday night." In the build-up to the fight, the 31-year-old Navarrete taunted Foster saying maybe he'll stick his chin out and let his opponent get in a good shot just so he can turn the fight into a war, instead of a more technical fight. Upon hearing that, Bobby Benton, Foster's trainer and owner of Houston's Main Street Gym, put his hands together in prayer, hoping Navarrete will actually try that route. "If he puts his chin out there like that, he'll go to sleep," Benton said. Foster, who is a slight favorite in the fight, laughs off any such talk. "It sounded good when he said it, but when you watch him fight, he doesn't even do that for those other guys," Foster said. "He doesn't really like getting hit in my opinion. He'll trade with you, but we'll see. If he does that, it'll be a great night for me, I'm not going to lie to you." For his part, Navarrete says he respects Foster's boxing ability, but is willing to do whatever it takes to open up the fight. "What I don't want is an entire night where we're just jabbing each other and we see who can jab more," Navarrete said. "I don't think the people want to see that fight. I think they want to see a good fight. They want to see a war.

Buffalo needs help in coverage, and the veteran cornerback offers a realistic way to improve the secondary without sacrificing an early selection. The fit deserves serious attention. Buffalo has championship ambitions, while Philadelphia must consider whether an expiring contract can become useful draft capital. Why Woolen would help Buffalo’s struggling defense Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The Bills rank 28th in defensive EPA per dropback making them one of the league’s worst pass defenes. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Woolen would not fix every problem. Linebacker positioning, safety communication and the pass rush would still require attention. However, adding another capable outside corner could reduce the number of vulnerable matchups opponents can target. At 6-foot-4, Woolen brings unusual length to the boundary. That gives him the physical tools to challenge outside receivers, disrupt throwing windows and contest passes that smaller defenders might struggle to reach. He also offers experience rather than an extended development project. Woolen started 59 career games through Week 6, including all six appearances for Philadelphia this season. He has recorded 24 tackles, four passes defended and a forced fumble in 2026. His interception total is zero, but Buffalo should evaluate more than takeaways. Reliable coverage can force quarterbacks away from their first read, buy time for rushers and make third downs harder to convert. There is a transition risk. The broadcast team failed to acknowledge that the course design and the Atlantic wind were the true villains, not the rookie’s swing. This approach disrespects the intelligence of the audience who knows that Port Royal Golf Course is a trap when the breeze picks up. Kevin Yu teed off in the third group at 6:57 a.m. ET, paired with Cam Davis and Lucas Glover, as noted by Golf.com . The hole in question is a par 4 where the wind can turn a simple drive into a nightmare. A stiff breeze can quickly change the leaderboard, a fact that should have been central to the analysis rather than a footnote. item.title: McDermott calls for Super League to accept NRL investment
item.description: Brian McDermott enjoyed a trophy-laden spell as Leeds Rhinos coach between 2011-18 [Getty Images] England head coach Brian McDermott has called for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game. Talks are currently ongoing after Super League clubs rejected a £35m package from the Australian Rugby League Commission and a second deadline of 15 October was allowed to pass without an agreement being reached. Formalising a partnership between the sport's two leading competitions is seen as as a key step in helping to grow the European competition's revenue. "I think the NRL's investment in Super League could be very, very positive," said McDermott, who is also the assistant coach of the Gold Coast Titans. "The product's brilliant. It has always being brilliant. The product's never been the problem. The players have never been the problem. The coaches have never been the problem. "It's just how it's marketed and how it's presented to people. I think there's some dominoes could start falling our way if the NRL invests and we accept their investment." Super League is yet to agree a new title sponsorship deal, finalise broadcast negotiations or even its fixtures for the 2027 campaign with London Broncos' position yet to be fully determined. The Broncos came in 16th on the yearly grading list, below fellow Championship side Barrow Raiders, despite a season in which they won the second tier's Grand Final, the 1895 Cup and were runaway champions in the regular-season standings. The Broncos were overlooked 12 months ago when Bradford Bulls, York Knights and Toulouse Olympique joined the expanded 14-team competition. But with the backing of Australian businessman Grant Wechsel and former Brisbane Broncos star Darren Lockyer, and with a squad full of internationals, they do still harbour hopes of playing in Super League in 2027. It is understood any completed deal would involve the Australian governing body insisting on Broncos featuring in the top flight in the near future. The financial gulf between the northern and southern hemisphere's elite competitions was laid bare, when the NRL struck a record A$5.3bn (£2.78bn) television deal over seven years in July. Super League's TV deal with Sky Sports, which expired at the end of 2026, was worth around £21.5m per year. "I know there's some positive notes around Super League at the moment, especially with crowds," McDermott added. "It would be a real positive validation of Super League if the NRL were to invest." item.title: Sage delighted to have Mateta back scoring for Crystal Palace
item.description: Sage delighted to have Mateta back scoring for Crystal Palace Pierre Sage praised Jean-Philippe Mateta’s return to scoring after netting in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas. Mateta played an hour on his first start since returning from injury and Sage says his return can be a huge boost for Palace. “I’m really happy for him,” Sage said. “He was in a good area, it was a good moment for him just before coming off, because he was not really ready to play [a full 90 minutes]. “You see him tired, but when you have this mindset, when you want to play every ball and you give your life on the pitch, sometimes it’s good for you.” Sage also praised the performance of his side, despite Palace letting a 2-1 lead slip. “We have a lot of satisfactions with the individual performances,” he said. “But I have to underline that, first of all, it’s about the collective performance. “They’re willing to play, they’re willing to go forward, they’re willing to press. “And I think at the end, they made a good game, without the deserved result.” The Palace boss was left frustrated by lapses in concentration which ultimately cost his side. “I am satisfied with the performance,” he added. “A little bit frustrated for the lads, because they gave a lot this evening and I think they deserve better. “We lacked concentration in the final minute of the first half, at the end. It was the same thing when we were 2-1 up. “In this kind of situation, you pay quickly if you make a little mistake.”

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. You can only beat what lies in front of you and Marco Rose’s players never relinquished control against a rotten impersonation of a Milan side. The visitors resembled holograms even before Mike Maignan, their goalkeeper, rendered their task impossible with a deserved sending-off in the first half. By then Justin Kluivert had given Bournemouth the lead with a penalty and it was another spot-kick from Marcus Tavernier, given after Maignan’s rush of blood, that underlined their overwhelming superiority. Amine Adli applied the garnish with a late free-kick and it meant an abject return to British shores for Ruben Amorim, who would have been excused seeing this particular week as the opportunity to make a point. On this evidence Manchester United, to whom Bournemouth travel on Sunday, share more than a few similarities with the modern version of Milan. Continue reading...

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
